title: Realizing I'd Been Taking Credit Without Meaning To
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] It took an uncomfortable comment from a junior colleague to make me realize I'd been unintentionally taking credit for work that wasn't entirely mine.
Narrator: During a client presentation, I described a strategy as something I had developed, when in reality it had emerged from a brainstorm with two other people.
Narrator: [carefully] I hadn't meant to erase their contribution deliberately; I'd simply told the story the way it existed in my own memory, which flattered me by default.
Narrator: Afterward, Wina, who had contributed the original idea, mentioned quietly that she'd noticed her name hadn't come up once during the entire meeting.
Narrator: [reflective] My immediate reaction was to explain myself, insisting it hadn't been intentional, as though intention were the only thing that mattered here.
Narrator: But sitting with it overnight, I recognized that impact matters regardless of intention, and the impact on Wina had been real, even if unintended.
Narrator: [honestly] I'd been the one presenting, the one visible in every meeting, so naturally the story kept collapsing into a version where I was the sole author.
Narrator: The next morning, I emailed the client directly, correcting the record and naming both colleagues as co-authors of the strategy we'd pitched.
Narrator: [gently] It felt oddly exposing to admit publicly that I'd gotten something wrong, as though correcting it drew even more attention to the original mistake.
Narrator: Instead, the client simply thanked me for the clarification, and Wina later told me it meant more to her than I probably realized at the time.
Narrator: [calmly] Since then, I've started deliberately naming contributors before presentations even begin, rather than trusting memory to distribute credit fairly on its own.
Narrator: It turns out memory is a fairly self-serving narrator, quietly editing out whoever wasn't standing at the front of the room.
Narrator: [encouraging] I don't think I'm a fundamentally dishonest person, but I've learned that fairness sometimes requires deliberate correction, not just good intentions left unexamined.
Narrator: Wina and I still work together closely, and if anything, the correction seemed to deepen her trust rather than damage my credibility.

quiz.question: What triggered the narrator's realization?
options: An uncomfortable comment from a junior colleague, Wina, about being uncredited
A performance review
A client complaint
A formal investigation
quiz.explanation: An uncomfortable comment from Wina, noting her name hadn't come up in the meeting, triggered the realization.

quiz.question: What had the narrator done during the client presentation?
options: Refused to present at all
Described a strategy as her own creation when it had come from a brainstorm with others
Blamed Wina for a mistake
Cancelled the meeting
quiz.explanation: She described the strategy as something she had developed, when it actually emerged from a brainstorm with two other people.

quiz.question: What was the narrator's first reaction when Wina mentioned it?
options: Immediate apology
Ignoring the comment completely
Defensively explaining that it hadn't been intentional
Firing Wina
quiz.explanation: Her immediate reaction was to explain herself defensively, insisting it hadn't been intentional.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do the next morning?
options: Nothing changed
Apologized privately but said nothing to the client
Asked Wina to stay quiet
Emailed the client to correct the record and name both colleagues as co-authors
quiz.explanation: She emailed the client directly, correcting the record and naming both colleagues as co-authors of the strategy.

quiz.question: What has the narrator changed going forward?
options: She avoids presenting entirely
She stopped working with Wina
She lets others take all the credit
She deliberately names contributors before presentations rather than trusting memory
quiz.explanation: She now deliberately names contributors before presentations begin, rather than trusting memory to distribute credit fairly.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator's memory overstate personal ownership of the strategy?
options: Ratna, I've been staring at these expense reports for an hour
I nearly cried in a meeting yesterday
Being the visible presenter made other contributions easier to forget.
Correct orders, inform customers, and equip support staff.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Being the visible presenter made other contributions easier to forget.

quiz.question: What did the narrator do after recognising the impact on Wina?
options: The client received a correction naming both colleagues as co-authors.
That's a fairly specific inconsistency to stumble across by accident
Here, someone just said the report was disorganized, full stop
It recorded evidence, actions, ownership, and corrective commitments.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The client received a correction naming both colleagues as co-authors.

quiz.question: How did the client respond to the corrected attribution?
options: If I raise it and I'm wrong, I've damaged a relationship over nothing
The client accepted the clarification without questioning credibility.
It could just as easily be a lack of consideration for how comments land on the receiving end
Blame did not replace analysis of the system.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The client accepted the clarification without questioning credibility.

quiz.question: What does the narrator learn about good intentions and fairness?
options: Fair outcomes sometimes require deliberate correction, not innocent motives.
It's just a decision dressed up as caution
When you separate it that way, it does land differently
The review had not turned her into the symbol of failure.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Fair outcomes sometimes require deliberate correction, not innocent motives.

quiz.question: How did acknowledging shared credit affect trust with Wina?
options: I'm not condemning anyone, just refusing to pretend I didn't notice
The correction strengthened their working relationship.
I'll try responding to the content next time instead of reacting to the delivery immediately
Ask why one ordinary error travelled so far undetected.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The correction strengthened their working relationship.
